tasks.short: Confer on scientific projects and technical assistance

steps.what: Read current project evidence and the actual scientific or technical questions for discussion
inputs: actual current project status and research records
participants' stated questions
outputs: checked discussion brief and evidence gaps

steps.what: Confer with scientists, engineers, regulators or others to plan, review or provide technical assistance
inputs: checked discussion brief and evidence gaps
participants' actual questions and responses
outputs: actual discussion outcomes and agreed follow-up

steps.what: Capture actual technical advice, decisions, owners and unresolved questions after the discussion
inputs: actual discussion outcomes and agreed follow-up

steps.what: Prepare a follow-up message from the recorded outcomes and verified participant contacts
inputs: complete actual discussion record draft
verified participant recipients and disclosure permissions
outputs: complete follow-up message with exact recipients

steps.what: Approve the completed record and exact follow-up message and recipients
inputs: complete actual discussion record draft
complete follow-up message with exact recipients
outputs: approved final discussion record and follow-up message

steps.what: Send the exact approved follow-up message to the approved participants
inputs: approved final discussion record and follow-up message

steps.what: Save the approved discussion record in the project file
inputs: approved final discussion record and follow-up message

tasks.design: Configure current project views in {PROJECT} and source-linked briefs in {DOCS}, with a native follow-up template in {EMAIL}. The manager conducts the discussion and records actual advice before the completed record and exact message are approved; send and save remain separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing current project evidence and formatting follow-up can repeat work around a substantive technical discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project filters and message templates can reuse checked evidence and actual recorded outcomes.
tasks.still_hard: Scientific disagreement, regulatory uncertainty and deciding what advice is justified require people.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands the participants' constraints and can challenge an unsupported technical assumption.

ambition.what: Review a project's unresolved scientific questions with current evidence more often.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1–4 for research access and participant disclosure rules

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: project views and document or email templates can prepare current evidence and format follow-up from captured outcomes.

assumptions: Shares and savings are provisional, not an observed baseline.
Project owners already maintain actual status; absent updates must be obtained and counted, not inferred.
Actual outcomes are captured by the manager in s3; no transcript or structured commitment arrives for free.
This scenario includes an outside participant, so s6 is external; an internal-only message uses internal-write authority.
Native configuration first. Short send and same-system save receive no saving.
research_questions: Which evidence preparation remains repetitive after native project views?

already_counted.description: Check final record and exact follow-up message

incremental.description: Maintain project views and follow-up template fields

approvals.approved_version: approved exact follow-up message and recipients; changes return to s5
approved final discussion record from s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 8 brief-preparation hours +5 message-assembly hours =13. One upkeep hour gives central net 12%; three extra hours reconciling stale status gives high 9%. Low zero if native configuration already covers these steps.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop client relationships and explain scientific work

steps.what: Check actual client commitments, specifications and relationship context
inputs: existing client contact and commitment records
actual current project status

steps.what: Prepare client discussion materials from approved proposals, findings and status
inputs: checked client and project context
approved proposal terms, research findings and disclosure limits

steps.what: Develop the client relationship and discuss proposals, findings, specifications or project status
inputs: checked discussion materials
actual client questions, preferences and concerns
outputs: actual client responses and agreed or unresolved points

steps.what: Record actual client requirements, responses and commitments without treating proposals as accepted
inputs: actual client responses and agreed or unresolved points
outputs: complete actual client discussion record draft

steps.what: Prepare a client follow-up message using the recorded actual agreements and exact client recipients
inputs: complete actual client discussion record draft
verified client contacts
outputs: complete client follow-up message and recipients

steps.what: Approve the completed client record and exact follow-up message against the actual discussion
inputs: complete actual client discussion record draft
complete client follow-up message and recipients
outputs: approved final client record and follow-up message

steps.what: Send the approved exact follow-up message to the client
inputs: approved final client record and follow-up message

steps.what: Save the approved client discussion record
inputs: approved final client record and follow-up message

tasks.design: Configure a client context view in {CRM} and reusable approved discussion materials in {DOCS}. The manager builds the relationship and captures actual requirements, then checks a templated follow-up in {EMAIL} before its separate send and the separate record save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing client context and repeatedly formatting approved project material can take time around relationship work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native client/project views and reusable material templates can reuse checked facts.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, negotiation and recognising misunderstood scientific claims remain human.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can distinguish a polite response from agreement and explain the limits of a finding.

ambition.what: Prepare a suitable scientific discussion for another authorised client audience.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1–4 for client and research disclosure permissions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: CRM views and reusable project-material templates can prepare client context and follow-up without replacing relationship conversations.

assumptions: This is a provisional work scenario, not measured current client-management effort.
Existing records contain actual client commitments and current status; s4 captures new actual requirements and responses.
The manager reviews scientific meaning and disclosure suitability while preparing s2, and approves the final written follow-up in s6.
Native features first; no saving in the client conversation, actual record capture, send or same-system save.
A later contractual acceptance or scope change needs its own authority and is not inferred from this discussion.
research_questions: Which preparation fields can be reused without misrepresenting client agreement?

already_counted.description: Approve the final client record and exact follow-up

incremental.description: Maintain client context links and approved material templates

approvals.approved_version: approved exact client follow-up and recipients; changes return to s6
approved final client discussion record from s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 6 context hours +6 material-preparation hours +2.8 follow-up hours =14.8. Upkeep 1.8 gives central net 13%; four additional hours checking client-specific disclosure gives high 9%. Low zero with existing native coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set scientific goals and detailed plans

steps.what: Interpret top management's actual strategic outlines and scientific constraints
inputs: top management's actual strategic outlines
known scientific and organisational constraints
outputs: understood strategic intent and open questions

steps.what: Review actual research capacity, project commitments and available resource evidence
inputs: existing project commitments and resource availability
actual approved budgets

steps.what: Determine scientific or technical goals and choose priorities, success criteria and trade-offs
inputs: understood strategic intent and open questions
checked planning evidence and gaps
outputs: human-chosen goals, priorities and success criteria

steps.what: Develop detailed milestones, dependencies, owners and resource plans in a reusable project structure
inputs: human-chosen goals, priorities and success criteria
checked planning evidence and gaps

steps.what: Check and approve the completed detailed plan against actual priorities, capacity and dependencies
inputs: complete detailed scientific project plan
human-chosen goals, priorities and success criteria

steps.what: Save the approved detailed scientific plan
inputs: approved final detailed scientific plan

tasks.design: Configure planning evidence views from {PROJECT} and {ERP}, then use a reusable milestone and dependency structure in {PROJECT}. The manager chooses the goals and actual detailed plan; the reduction in plan preparation is limited to reused fields, dependency display and formatting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reviewing current commitments and repeatedly arranging project-plan fields can slow detailed planning.
tasks.enabler_now: Native resource views and reusable project structures can make known constraints visible while the manager plans.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing scientific goals under uncertainty and reconciling competing priorities requires accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can change the goal when the evidence shows that the original aim is infeasible.

ambition.what: Revisit scientific plans when actual capacity or evidence changes.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1–4 for resource and budget access, with team consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: project tools can display resource commitments and reuse milestone/dependency structures while people retain goal and plan decisions.

assumptions: Shares are provisional scenario choices, not the prompt's time-share prior or measured planning effort.
Project owners maintain actual commitments; no tool invents capacity or treats an unconfirmed owner as committed.
s4 retains 70% effort for actual detailed planning and capture; only repeated field setup and display formatting are reduced.
Native configuration first. Saving in the same project system has no saving.
Other proposal and project-planning tasks may overlap; reconcile a role roll-up instead of adding their savings without checking.
research_questions: How much detailed planning is substantive choice rather than repeated field setup?

already_counted.description: Check the complete plan against chosen goals and actual capacity

incremental.description: Maintain planning views, field defaults and dependency templates

approvals.approved_version: approved final detailed scientific plan; edits return to s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 8 evidence-preparation hours +7.2 plan-setup hours =15.2. Upkeep 2.2 gives central net 13%; four extra hours reconciling resource exceptions gives high 9%. Low zero if native planning features already cover this work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify the actual project request, audience and proposal requirements
inputs: actual project request and proposal requirements
requester's actual constraints
outputs: confirmed proposal scope and required sections

steps.what: Check actual supporting research, capacity and cost evidence for the proposal
inputs: existing approved research findings
actual resource commitments and approved cost rates
confirmed proposal scope and required sections
outputs: checked proposal evidence and explicit gaps

steps.what: Design the proposed scientific approach, deliverables, assumptions, timeline and resource request
inputs: confirmed proposal scope and required sections
checked proposal evidence and explicit gaps
outputs: human-authored technical approach and proposed commitments

steps.what: Draft the complete project proposal using approved evidence and the manager's actual technical design
inputs: human-authored technical approach and proposed commitments
checked proposal evidence and explicit gaps
confirmed proposal scope and required sections

loop.purpose: Propose readable proposal wording from the manager's supplied design
loop.input: human-authored technical approach, checked evidence and required proposal sections
loop.output: complete proposal prose draft with source links and explicit gaps
loop.check: Manager checks scientific meaning, feasibility, unsupported claims, omissions and all commitments against the supplied design; arithmetic is deterministic
loop.stop: Missing cost, evidence or commitment returns to the manager; no invented findings, citations or promises
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates populate fixed fields but do not express the variable supplied scientific approach in prose

steps.what: Review and correct the complete proposal for scientific validity, costs, feasibility and actual commitments
inputs: complete source-linked proposal draft
human-authored technical approach and proposed commitments
checked proposal evidence and explicit gaps

steps.what: Approve the exact completed proposal as ready for the organisation's required submission process
inputs: corrected complete final project proposal

steps.what: Save the approved prepared proposal in the controlled project folder
inputs: approved final prepared project proposal

tasks.design: Configure checked evidence views from {PROJECT} and {ERP} and a proposal template in {DOCS}. After the manager designs the actual project, a bounded model step proposes source-linked wording; the manager checks the full version and saves it for the required submission process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence preparation and drafting readable proposal prose can take time after the substantive project design exists.
tasks.enabler_now: Native data views and a bounded source-grounded drafting step can reuse a complete human-authored design.
tasks.still_hard: Scientific novelty, feasibility, risk and credible commitments remain the manager's responsibility.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can reject a persuasive proposal that the team cannot deliver.

ambition.what: Prepare another evidence-grounded project option without bypassing scientific review.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2–5 for confidential research and budget access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document templates and source-grounded model drafting can express a supplied technical design while a person checks scientific claims and commitments.

assumptions: All effort shares and savings are provisional scenarios, not measured proposal-writing baselines.
Actual findings, rates and capacity records already exist; missing facts remain gaps and are not supplied by the model.
The manager authors the technical design in s3. Drafting does not choose objectives or create commitments.
Native template and evidence views are configured first. Submission is a distinct authorised action after the prepared proposal; no submission saving is assumed.
The same-folder save is approximately zero today and receives no saving. Reconcile overlap with detailed project planning before role aggregation.
unknowns: Completeness of cost and research evidence
research_questions: Does source-grounded wording assistance reduce net drafting effort after full technical review?

already_counted.description: Review all scientific claims, costs and commitments in the completed draft

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings and proposal templates and sample drafting errors

approvals.approved_version: approved final prepared project proposal; edits require renewed s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 6 evidence-preparation hours +12.5 drafting hours =18.5. Upkeep 2.5 gives central net 16%; four extra hours correcting scientific wording gives high 12%. Low zero if current templates already cover drafting or review absorbs the reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: scientists and engineers: validate technical evidence
clients and project participants: confirm actual requirements
role.ambitious_version: A scientific manager with faster preparation of evidence and documents, retaining direct ownership of goals, relationships and scientific commitments.
